answers.M8-S1: The author tests whether Mason-bees can find their way home after being carried two and a half miles away, and some return quickly despite hard conditions.
answers.M8-S2: To show the bees faced an extra difficulty: flying low against the wind, they couldn't see the landscape, which makes their quick return more surprising.
answers.M8-S3: The trip was easy enough for them that they stopped to gather pollen along the way, so they found home with time to spare, not struggling.
answers.M8-S4: So he could recognize them when they reached the nest and know they were his released bees, not other bees that lived there.
answers.M8-S5: He goes from doubting any bees would make it back, given injuries and the wind, to learning two returned fast, which surprises and proves his question.
answers.M8-S6: In time order, as an account of an experiment: setting it up, marking and releasing the bees, the conditions, and then the result at home.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast and impressive the return was: two and a half miles in under forty-five minutes, even with time to stop and forage.
answers.M8-S8: To show the experiment was hard and imperfect; injured bees might not return, so fewer bees could be expected home, adding to his doubts.
answers.M8-S9: That they couldn't find home by looking at landmarks from above, so they must have used some other way of knowing the route.
